newsitem.title: USA: King County, Wash., damage estimate is $97 million.
newsitem.headline: King County, Wash., damage estimate is $97 million.

text.p: King County suffered an estimated $97.5 million in damage from snow and flooding in the recent holiday storm including $47 million to public facilities, officials said Friday.

The city of Seattle was hardest hit with $20.3 million in damage to public facilities including a major bridge that had to be closed indefinitely after it was hit by a massive mud slide that knocked out steel support beams.
Damage to homes and businesses in the county was estimated at $50.5 million, with about $27.6 million uninsured.

"Because many home and business owners have not reported their losses, the final total for the county is expected to rise significantly from these early estimates," the county's Office of Emergency Management said.
Gov. Mike Lowry is gathering damage estimates from across the state and is expected to file a formal request for federal disaster assistance before he leaves office Tuesday.
A series of winter storms battered the state the week between Christmas and New Year's Day, triggering mud slides, undermining roadways and causing widespread flooding.
